strongest_angle: Comparing the divine attributes, familial origins from Cronus and Rhea, and distinct cosmic realms of Zeus and Poseidon using classical mythological sources.

key_facts.fact: Zeus and Poseidon are brothers born to Cronus and Rhea, who worked with their siblings and the Cyclopes to overthrow Cronus and take dominion over Mount Olympus and the universe.
According to Homeric accounts referenced in Perseus Tufts, Zeus dwelt on Mount Olympus in Thessaly and held supreme sovereignty as the father of gods and men whom all immortals obey.
Poseidon is recognized as the Olympian god of the Mediterranean sea, earthquakes, floods, and drought, distinguished by his iconic three-pronged fisherman's spear known as the trident.
In the division of cosmic realms among the brothers, Zeus received the sky and weather, while Poseidon was assigned lordship over the sea and the fluid element.
